research_objective: Understand how people in different life situations relate to grocery delivery — what they value, what frustrates them, and how they think about its place in daily life.
topic_domain: Consumer attitudes toward grocery delivery services
participant_collective_identity: consumers with varying experiences of grocery delivery services
moderator_knowledge_brief: Grocery delivery services (like Ocado, Tesco, Sainsbury's, Deliveroo, etc.) became highly prominent, especially during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Key tensions include: convenience vs. cost/markup, quality of substituted items, loss of control over choosing fresh products, lack of social interactions, and physical disconnect from food/local businesses. Explore these dimensions naturally.
researcher_notes: Pay attention to differences in attitude based on age and family situation. Observe if they discuss the social and economic dimensions (e.g., gig economy, disconnection from food sources). Invite quiet participants like Daniel when appropriate.

participants.name: Maya Chen
participants.profile_summary: Maya Chen is a 28-year-old female UX designer living alone in urban Manchester. Upper-middle income. Personality: High openness (0.80) and extraversion (0.75), moderate conscientiousness (0.55) and agreeableness (0.50), low neuroticism (0.35). Values: self-direction, stimulation, achievement. Thinking style: intuitive. Backstory: Uses grocery delivery 2-3 times a week, mainly because of long working hours. Sees it as a basic part of modern city life. Confident, opinionated, comfortable disagreeing with others.

participants.name: Robert Hayes
participants.profile_summary: Robert Hayes is a 64-year-old retired secondary school teacher. Lives in suburban outskirts of Bristol, married with grown children. Income bracket: middle. Psychological profile: Openness: 0.55, Conscientiousness: 0.80, Extraversion: 0.55, Agreeableness: 0.65, Neuroticism: 0.40. Values: tradition, benevolence, security. Thinking style: effortful. Backstory: Tried Ocado a few times during the pandemic, went back to weekly trips to Sainsbury's. Misses the social aspect of shopping — chatting with the butcher, running into neighbours. Thoughtful, doesn't speak first but pushes back when he disagrees.

participants.name: Priya Sharma
participants.profile_summary: Priya Sharma is a 41-year-old NHS clinical pharmacist. Lives in urban Birmingham, married with two children aged 6 and 9. Income bracket: upper-middle. Psychological profile: Openness: 0.70, Conscientiousness: 0.75, Extraversion: 0.60, Agreeableness: 0.70, Neuroticism: 0.45. Values: benevolence, achievement, universalism. Thinking style: effortful. Backstory: Uses delivery for weekly staples (bulky items, household goods) but always shops in person for fresh produce and meat. Pragmatic, sees both sides of most arguments, often the person who bridges disagreements in groups.

participants.name: Daniel Whitmore
participants.profile_summary: Daniel Whitmore is a 35-year-old self-employed electrician. Lives in rural-edge suburban small town outside Sheffield, married with one child aged 3. Income bracket: lower-middle. Psychological profile: Openness: 0.45, Conscientiousness: 0.65, Extraversion: 0.35, Agreeableness: 0.55, Neuroticism: 0.60. Values: security, tradition, self-direction. Thinking style: intuitive. Backstory: Tried a delivery service once when his wife was ill, found the markup excessive and the substitutions frustrating. Suspicious of the pricing. Quiet by nature, contributes when invited or when something genuinely annoys him.

discussion_guide.section_purpose: Welcome and introductions. Get all participants speaking and comfortable sharing details of their lives.
discussion_guide.scripted_question: Welcome, everyone. Today we're talking about grocery delivery — the apps and services that bring food to your door. There are no right answers here; I'm just interested in your honest experiences and views. Let's start by going around briefly so we know who's in the room.

discussion_guide.section_purpose: First main topic question: tell me about a time you used a grocery delivery service. What made it work well, or where did it fall short?
discussion_guide.scripted_question: Tell me about a time you used a grocery delivery service. What made it work well, or where did it fall short?

discussion_guide.section_purpose: Second main topic question: infrastructure vs luxury, disconnection from food sources.
discussion_guide.scripted_question: Some people say grocery delivery has become essential infrastructure for modern life. Others say it's a luxury that's quietly disconnecting us from what we eat and the people who grow it. Where do you land on that, and why?

discussion_guide.section_purpose: Capture any closing thoughts and wind down the discussion.
discussion_guide.scripted_question: Before we finish, is there anything else about grocery delivery or the way we get our food that you'd like to share?
